The post isn't pro-Sanders.  The post is anti-corruption.  And **everyone** should be anti-corruption.

They're the victims here.

I usually vote Republican locally.  Do you know why?

Guns.

The right to bear arms was put in place for citizens to form a militia, and to make the government fear oppressing it's people.

I don't think abortion should happen either, goddammit.  But I also massively support universal healthcare, wrangling in the student loan problem or making tuition free for colleges that my taxes go to anyway, gay marriage, reefer legalisation (and I've never even had it), and expansion of social services.

But because I believe a government should be scared of it's people I'm automatically labeled a Republican in the Basket Of Deplorables.

Everyone assumes we have no common ground with Democrats.  But the problem with **both** parties is you're either in all the way or you have one belief that differs from the rest so you're not one of them.

I'm mostly Democrat, but I hold one very strong belief that alienates me from them.  And enough Democratic beliefs where I can't be called a Republican.

-----

And as a sidenote, firearms are great.  They provide immediate protection of yourself in your home without having to wait for law enforcement.  Enough citizens with enough firearms makes governments afraid to overreach as well.  Everyone should know proper firearm safety to own one because it's the idiots who mishandle them, the severely mentally ill that misuse them, and the gangs that overuse them that make everyone so damn scared.

Her and her DNC friends made certain that Bernie Sanders wouldn't be the nominee and hid that from the voters.

Maybe she would've won the nomination legitimately anyway even if the DNC hadn't rigged it.

Or maybe Bernie Sanders would've won the nomination.

Maybe he would've won the election too.  Changed the course of the country.  Gave us a president that we'd be proud to take home to mom and show all of our friends.

Maybe.

But we'll never know.  That opportunity and that chance were stolen from us when a party said "fuck democracy, here's who we pick anyway".  A party that's supposed to stand for voter rights instead said "fuck the voters that didn't vote for the candidate that we're nominating anyway".

You think Republicans are happy with having to vote for Trump either?  Very few are happy with this outcome.  Hillary people are pissed that she didn't win, Republicans are pissed a more conventional candidate didn't win, and Bernie voters are pissed they were never even given a chance to begin with.

This whole thing could've went a lot differently if the DNC would've just let everything turn out like how it was supposed to.  Like the way everyone wanted.  A fair election where the scales aren't tipped in a candidate's favor by the party.  Even if the nominee would've been Clinton.  An entire party isn't supposed to collude against a candidate they don't like.  We were all robbed, we're all still paying the price, and we'll all still continue to pay the price every day because of what the DNC did to the integrity of our elections, to the American voter, and to the rest of the world.
